MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 6, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of
the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 pm,
on September 6, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 2, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  W. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Mayor Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

  CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of
  City Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

  CS2. Labor Negotiations—The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor
  Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the
City Council Minutes  1  September 6, 2011
   Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered two items in Closed Session
but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

  P1. Recognition of Denise Matson by the 2011 Relay for Life Committee for her
  Planning and Organization Efforts of the Cancer Prevention Study (CPS-3)

  Mayor Leckness and the 2011 Relay for Life Committee presented a plaque to
  Denise Matson for her efforts in coordinating the 2011 Cancer Prevention Study
  (CPS-3).

  P2. Certificates of Appreciation to Margot Ferron and Cathy Allen of the Mission
  Viejo Activities Committee for Their Fund Raising Efforts Supporting Joplin,
  Missouri

  Mayor Leckness presented certificates of appreciation to Margot Ferron and Cathy
  Allen.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Maurer, M.V.: introduced Husker, a trained therapy dog, who helps children practice their
reading skills at the Mission Viejo library.

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that the new City Outlook magazine paints a rosy financial picture
for the City and he feels that is inaccurate.

Dan Avery, M.V.: announced that the new Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce is underway.
He encouraged residents to visit www.missionviejochamber.com to register for an invitation to
view the site when it is complete.

Christine Saracino, M.V.: expressed concern with ongoing construction at 26992 La Paja Lane
after neighbors were promised a completion date of December 2009. She asked for updates on
the construction at that property and another home on the same street.

City Council Minutes  2  September 6, 2011
 Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: thanked the City Council for the way they support the City's kids and
for the crossing guards that the City provides. She also encouraged residents to attend the
Patriots Day ceremony on September 11, 2011.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 5, 7 and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated August 5, 2011 in the amount of $533,224.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated August 12, 2011 in the amount of $901,659.48

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Amendment to Schedule of Fines and Fees for the Mission Viejo Library

  Adopted Library Resolution 11-01 Amending the Schedule of Fines and Fees for the
  Mission Viejo Library.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  9.  Appeal filed by Mayor Dave Leckness and Council Member Cathy Schlicht of
  the Planning and Transportation Commission’s July 11, 2011 approval of
  Planned Development Permit PDP2009-219, being a petition submitted by Chris
  Livoni of Watermarke Properties, Inc. to construct a 256-unit multifamily
  residential apartment development (Andalucia Mission Viejo) on a 7.12-acre
  vacant site south of the intersection of Oso Parkway and Montanoso Drive, in the
  City’s RPD 30A (Residential Planned Development by Right) zone. The subject
  site is located adjacent to Sunrise Assisted Living and Mission Viejo Country
City Council Minutes  3  September 6, 2011
   Club. The proposed project consists of three, 3- to 4-story buildings with an
  average height of approximately 45 feet. The proposed development consists of
  two distinct communities designed to operate independently, or as one
  community sharing common area facilities. These developments are located on
  either side of Oso Creek and are connected via a foot bridge crossing the creek.
  The proposed project also includes Oso Creek improvements consisting of
  stabilization of the creek banks as well as re-vegetation and restoration. This
  7.12-acre site is identified as a potential affordable housing site in the City’s
  General Plan Housing Element. Of the development’s 256 units, 38 units are
  proposed as affordable at very low and low income. The applicant has applied
  for a "density bonus" to increase project density approximately 20% over the
  otherwise maximum allowable residential density in accordance with state and
  local law

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Elaine Lister, Planning and Economic Development Manager, provided an overview
  of housing element law and presented background on the property. She also displayed
  a site plan, elevations and a photo simulation of the proposed multi-family apartment
  building.

  All five City Council Members indicated that they have driven by or visited the site of
  the proposed project and disclosed any meetings, conversations and/or
  correspondence they have exchanged on the project.

  Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing at 7:04 p.m.

  Greg Neville, Watermarke Properties, Inc.: outlined the proposed project and
  presented images depicting the building design, the site plan, and the style of the
  architecture.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed apartment complex: David
  D’Altorio, M.V.; Fred Pack, M.V.; Gene Insley, M.V.; Judy Soulakis, M.V.;
  Catherine Jasper, M.V.; Mary Pehkoff, M.V.; Larry Grills, M.V.; Deborah Stine,
  M.V.; Andrew McCarron, M.V.; Christine Saracino, M.V.; George Erickson, M.V.;
  Jeanette Noble, M.V.; , Dale Sandore, M.V.; Anthony Elia, M.V.; and Sue Sauer,
  M.V.

  The following spoke in support of the proposed apartment complex: Sam Dawly,
  M.V.; Sean Anderson, M.V.; Dan Avery, M.V.; Brad Shupe, General Manager of the
  Mission Viejo Country Club, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in opposition to the proposed project:
  Roberto Saracino, M.V. and Cindy and Michael Simon, M.V.

City Council Minutes  4  September 6, 2011
   Greg Neville, Watermarke Properties, Inc.: provided rebuttal comments and answered
  the City Council Member’s questions.

  The City Council Members asked questions of staff and of the developer.

  At the hour of 8:27 p.m., Mayor Leckness closed the public hearing.

  RECESS

  At the hour of 8:28 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess. The City Council reconvened
  at 8:40 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to confirm the
  Planning and Transportation Commission action by denying the appeal and adopting
  Resolution 11-56 Approving Planned Development Permit PDP2009-219, and by
  Adopting a Mitigated Negative Declaration for Proposed Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to continue
  items 2, 5, 7, and 8 until the next Council Meeting

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness
  ABSENT:  None

  2.  City Council Minutes

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

  5.  Check Register dated August 19, 2011 in the amount of $548,126.30

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

  7.  Transfer of Southern California Edison Rule 20A Allocations

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

City Council Minutes  5  September 6, 2011
   8.  La Paz Roadway and Bridge Widening Improvements (CIP 756/761)

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

OLD BUSINESS

  10. Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)

  Kelly Doyle, Director of Recreation and Community Services, presented the staff
  report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  award the Construction Contract to the lowest responsible bidder Western Alta
  Construction Company in the amount of $3,742,848 for the project; (2) reject the bid
  protest submitted by C.S. Legacy Construction; (3) approve Change Order No.1 to
  Friess Construction, Inc. for construction management services during the
  construction portion of the project in the amount of $80,232; (4) approve Change
  Order No. 3 to RJM Design Group for the bid process and
  Construction/Administration Services portion during the construction portion of the
  project in the amount $97,250; (5) approve a Purchase Order with Petra
  Geotechnical, Incorporated for geotechnical field observations and inspections in the
  amount of $70,813; and (6) adopt Resolution 11-57 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-
  2012 Budget for Revenues and Costs Related to Capital Improvement Marguerite
  Tennis Center Project 501 for $975,000.

  The following expressed support for the proposed Tennis Center renovation project:
  Wil Garcia, M.V.; Jason Harnett, M.V.; and Wendy Bucknum, M.V.

  Written statements in support of the project were received from the following:
  Patricia Bennett, M.V.; Debra Griffith, M.V.; Del and Leslee Holt, M.V.; David
  Allen, M.V.; Cathy Allen, M.V.; Monica Dean, Rancho Santa Margarita; Beth Ng,
  Foothill Ranch; and Michael Chang, M.V.

  A petition bearing signatures of 22 supporters of the project was presented to the City
  Clerk.

  The City Council Members asked questions of staff and of Ken Friess, construction
  manager.

  Amended motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member
  Schlicht, to award a construction contract for Phase I of the project only, which
  would include replacement of the existing tennis building, the adjacent plaza
  area, new lighting for the tennis courts, and resurfacing of the existing tennis courts
  and spectator seating.

  On roll call, said AMENDED motion failed by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  6  September 6, 2011
   AYES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, Leckness and Ury
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to move
  the previous question to (1) award the Construction Contract to the lowest
  responsible bidder Western Alta Construction Company in the amount of $3,742,848
  for the project; (2) reject the bid protest submitted by C.S. Legacy Construction; (3)
  approve Change Order No.1 to Friess Construction, Inc. for construction
  management services during the construction portion of the project in the amount of
  $80,232; (4) approve Change Order No. 3 to RJM Design Group for the bid process
  and Construction/Administration Services portion during the construction portion of
  the project in the amount $97,250; (5) approve a Purchase Order with Petra
  Geotechnical, Incorporated for geotechnical field observations and inspections in the
  amount of $70,813; and (6) adopt Resolution 11-57 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-
  2012 Budget for Revenues and Costs Related to Capital Improvement Marguerite
  Tennis Center Project 501 for $975,000.

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

  11. Investment Advisory Commission Appointment

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  appoint Kyle Kamrooz to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley announced that she has not attended a recent meeting of the
  OCFA Board of Directors.

  13. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

City Council Minutes  7  September 6, 2011
   Mayor Pro Tem Ury postponed his report to the next City Council Meeting.

  14. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing new to report on the San Joaquin
  Hills TCA.

  15. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley announced that she was unable to attend the SCAG
  Committee meeting on September 1, 2011, therefore she does not have a report at
  this time.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

  16. Proposed Refunding of City of Mission Viejo Community Facilities District
  (CFD) 92-1 Special Tax Bonds

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon,
  to approve refunding of the City of Mission Viejo CFD 92-1 Special Tax Bonds
  under staff’s scenario #1 which will reduce the tax burden of the property owners.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

  17. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley invited the public to participate in a blood drive she is organizing on
Friday, September 9, 2011, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at City Hall.
She announced that she planned the blood drive to honor of the victims of September 11, 2001,
and Council Member Kelley encouraged residents to either call her for an appointment or sign up
City Council Minutes  8  September 6, 2011
 at www.redcrossblood.org, using the code COMV. She also invited the community to attend a
Patriots Day ceremony on September 11 at 8:00 a.m. at the Civic Center which will be led by
Boy Scout and Girl Scout troops. Additionally, Mission Viejo Christian Church is inviting the
community to come out and honor the victims of September 11 the same evening from 7:00 to
8:00 p.m. Council Member Kelley commended the City Manager and the Director of Public
Works for doing a great job on the Oso Parkway widening project and she noted that she has
heard similar comments from residents. Council Member Kelley also reminded the community
that school is starting tomorrow and she encouraged students to make the best of the school
year. Lastly, Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the
month of September is responsibility.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she attended the grand opening of the new Forever 21
store and also a special briefing of the ACCOC and Orange County Business Council where she
heard Fresno’s Mayor Swearengin speak. She noted that the Mayor is very humble and her
speech was quite impressive. Council Member Reardon also attended the business showcase last
Thursday and she commended staff member Karen Wylie on her efforts in planning such a
successful event. Council Member Reardon reminded residents to continue praying for 5 year-
old Cade Spinello who has a brain tumor, is undergoing chemotherapy, and also recovering from
a stroke.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked Mayor Leckness to conclude the meeting in memory of Bill
Faulds. She also discussed the tragedy on September 11, 2001, and she stated that on that day,
ordinary people did extraordinary things and the country will forever be grateful.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Leckness

  18. Oso Creek Trail Tour

  Mayor Leckness presented his report.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to set the date
  for a tour of the Oso Creek Trail for September 19, 2011, at 3:00 p.m., prior to the
  regular City Council meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  9  September 6, 2011
   Mayor Leckness discussed his attendance at the Forever 21 grand opening and he
  reminded his colleagues that the Robbins Brothers ribbon cutting event will be held on
  Thursday, September 8, 2011, at 6:00 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 11:14 p.m., with no further business to come before the Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Bill Faulds to Monday, September 19,
2011, at 3:00 p.m. (for a tour of the Oso Creek Trail.)

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 19, 2011

City Council Minutes  10  September 6, 2011
